subject: Contingent SLA coverage & monthly reconciliation mechanics
messages:
From: Michelle Park <michelle@tiltai.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Ajay Singh <ajay.procurement@tiltai.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA carveouts for scheduled batch windows + monthly credits mechanics

Hi Dylan / Ajay,

Thanks again for the demo last week — TiltAI is excited about Redwood's latency profile for inference. Before procurement signs anything we need to confirm a couple of operational items so we can get budget approval on our side. High level ask: we need an explicit option in the SLA template that permits a contingent coverage model for heavy scheduled batch workloads (analytics and model retraining inference) that runs outside our low-latency realtime tier. Specifically: 

- Availability target: TiltAI's procurement team will accept 99.5% monthly availability for the batch tier, but we expect the realtime production endpoints to remain at 99.9%.
- Measurement and reconciliation: monthly reconciliation of credits tied to actual usage (per-route, per-model) rather than a flat monthly credit.
- Latency: realtime 95th pctl SLO remains as discussed (<=350ms for <1k token requests); batch jobs should have a separate latency window (95th pctl <=2s) and be allowed scheduled windows where higher tail latency is expected.
- Credit cap: TiltAI needs a guarantee on maximum monthly credit exposure so our finance team can model worst-case.

Can Redwood draft language that: 1) includes a distinct "Batch Tier" carveout with separate availability/latency SLOs; 2) defines a monthly reconciliation mechanism using usage measurements; and 3) proposes a practical credit schedule tied to the tiered availability bands?

If you can send a short draft and example calculation, Ajay (cc'd) will route to finance. We prefer to keep legal review focused and move quickly if we can align on economics.

Thanks,
Michelle Park
CTO, TiltAI
[Attachment: tiltai_network_diagram.png (png, 240KB)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Park <michelle@tiltai.com>, Ajay Singh <ajay.procurement@tiltai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carveouts for scheduled batch windows + monthly credits mechanics

Michelle / Ajay — thanks, this is clear and a good starting point. We've put together a short amendment that implements a separate "Batch Tier" with distinct availability & latency bands, and a usage-based monthly reconciliation flow. I'm attaching a redline + a reconciliation spreadsheet showing example math for a $25k monthly invoice.

High level proposal (summary):
- Tiering: Realtime Tier (default) keeps the standard platform SLA: 99.9% monthly availability. Batch Tier (customer-declared scheduled windows) is eligible for a lower SLA of 99.5% for the duration of the declared schedule, with explicit configuration in the customer console.
- Credits (example bands):
  * Realtime Tier: availability <99.9% and >=99.5% => credit = 10% of monthly invoice prorated to impacted routes; <99.5% => credit = 30% prorated.
  * Batch Tier: availability <99.5% and >=99.0% => credit = 7% of batch-tier bill; <99.0% => credit = 20% of batch-tier bill.
- Credit cap / reconciliation: default cap = 25% of total monthly invoice; however, we propose an "opt-in" lower cap for TiltAI at 20% with an escalation clause: if credits exceed the cap for two consecutive months due to platform issues, Redwood will trigger a compensation review and offer service credits or temporary free dedicated capacity for a specified window. The reconciliation is usage-weighted (per-route token counts) and is performed monthly with a 30-day dispute window.
- Measurement & windows: availability measured per-route on a 30-day rolling window; batch windows are declared in the Console with start/end times and can be adjusted with 48hrs notice. Scheduled maintenance and customer-controlled jobs are explicitly excluded from credits if they fall within declared maintenance windows.
- Latency carveout: separate SLO for Batch Tier: 95th pctl <=2s. Credits tied to latency breaches are measured only for batch-declared routes.

Next steps I propose: 1) review the attached draft ("sla_amendment_draft.pdf") and the sample reconciliation spreadsheet, 2) confirm the credit cap TiltAI is comfortable with (we used 20% in the sample), and 3) if that aligns, we route the redline to Legal for final wording and then to procurement for signatures.

Attachments:
- sla_amendment_draft.pdf (draft redline, explains definitions and examples)
- usage-reconciliation-template.xlsx (example calculation)

If this looks directionally right I can get Ben in to discuss any commercial guardrails you want tightened.

Subject: Re: SLA carveouts for scheduled batch windows + monthly credits mechanics

Adding a quick commercial note from our side. The framework Dylan proposed is reasonable, but we should tighten two items before routing to Legal: 

1) Cap mechanics: suggest explicit hard cap at 20% monthly on platform credits, but allow a one-time "exception credit" in the event of a Sev1 caused entirely by Redwood (to be approved by Sales Ops). This protects our revenue while giving TiltAI recourse.
2) Measurement alignment: require a neutral measurement feed (we can provide salted telemetry export or CloudWatch/Prometheus peer metrics) for reconciliation to reduce disputes.

Also recommend removing any language that permits retrospective expansion of credit bands (that has been a negotiation pain in some large accounts). If TiltAI wants a lower cap, we can accept it but we'll need a mutually agreed SLA runbook and weekly digest during the first 90-day pilot so both teams can tune thresholds.

If you're okay with 20% + one-time exception clause, I'll draft a compact commercial term we can drop into the redline.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

From: Michelle Park <michelle@tiltai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ajay Singh <ajay.procurement@tiltai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carveouts for scheduled batch windows + monthly credits mechanics

Ben / Dylan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity in the draft. TiltAI is prepared to move forward on the following basis: 

- We accept the Batch Tier concept and the idea of separate bands.
- We can accept a 20% monthly credit cap, provided Redwood incorporates explicit language that scheduled maintenance windows and customer-declared batch runs are excluded only if they were declared per the Console workflow (48hrs notice) or documented in the runbook. Emergency maintenance that Redwood initiates without timely notice should not be excluded.
- Replace the term "automatic fallback" in the draft with an explicit "routing fallback policy" clause that spells out when Redwood will route to a secondary model/region and how that impacts credits. We need that to avoid surprise failovers that affect billing.
- For the pilot period (first 90 days after go-live) we want a weekly incident digest (rolling 7-day window) and a shared telemetry export (S3 or CloudWatch) for reconciliation; Ajay will make the final selection with your ops team.

Please strip out the phrase allowing Redwood to "retrospectively expand" credit bands — that's a non-starter for our finance team. If you can incorporate the three changes above and push the redline to DocuSign we will route to our legal and procurement. Ajay will look for the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Michelle Park
CTO, TiltAI
